title: White smoke + milky oil cap: head gasket warning signs

standingNegativePrompt: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.shot: Close-up: thick white smoke rolling continuously from a car tailpipe at idle, cold morning light
beats.prompt: close up shot of a car tailpipe at idle, thick white smoke rolling out continuously, cold morning light, condensation visible, photorealistic, cinematic
beats.vo: White tailpipe smoke that keeps going after warmup.

beats.shot: Close-up: engine oil filler cap being lifted off, revealing pale frothy milkshake-colored residue under the cap
beats.prompt: extreme close up of a car engine oil filler cap being lifted off, the underside coated in pale frothy milkshake-colored residue, engine bay lighting, macro detail, photorealistic
beats.vo: Pop the oil cap. A milkshake look can point to coolant mixing in.

beats.shot: Macro cutaway-style shot: cross-section of a head gasket surface with a visible gap between cylinder and coolant passage
beats.prompt: macro cutaway diagram-style shot of an engine cylinder head gasket surface, a visible thin gap between the cylinder bore and an adjacent coolant passage, clean technical lighting, photorealistic illustration style
beats.vo: The head gasket seals coolant and combustion apart.

beats.shot: Close-up: coolant reservoir tank with unusual bubbling / rising fluid level at idle
beats.prompt: close up of a translucent car coolant reservoir tank, coolant fluid visibly bubbling and slowly rising with the engine idling, engine bay background, photorealistic
beats.vo: Disappearing coolant, or bubbles in the overflow tank, is a second clue.

beats.shot: Close-up: exhaust tailpipe again, sweet-smelling steam-like vapor distinct from normal exhaust, sunlight backlighting the vapor
beats.prompt: close up backlit shot of vapor and light smoke exiting a car exhaust tailpipe, sunlight catching the vapor trail, outdoor daylight, photorealistic
beats.vo: It smells sweet, not like burnt oil.

beats.shot: Close-up: dipstick pulled and wiped clean against a white cloth, showing the oil's true color and texture
beats.prompt: close up of an engine oil dipstick being wiped against a white cloth, showing oil color and texture, garage lighting, photorealistic, no hands or human figures visible
beats.vo: Do not guess on one clue.

beats.shot: Wide static hold: clean, dry automotive service bay under bright shop lighting, no signage/logo visible
beats.prompt: wide static shot of a clean automotive service bay interior, bright even lighting, no visible signage, logos, or text, photorealistic, held static frame

ig_fb_copy.primaryCaption: White smoke from your tailpipe that doesn't clear after a minute? Check your oil cap — if it looks like a milkshake instead of black oil, that's coolant mixing in. One clue alone doesn't confirm it, but both together are worth a look. Stop by and we'll take a look.

adVariants.label: curiosity
adVariants.hook: That white smoke isn't always the weather.
adVariants.caption: Persistent white smoke plus a milky oil cap can point to coolant and oil mixing where they shouldn't. Two clues, one quick check.
adVariants.cta: Stop by and we'll take a look — no guessing.

adVariants.label: relatability
adVariants.hook: Pop your oil cap before your next oil change.
adVariants.caption: Frothy, pale residue under the cap is a clue worth checking — especially paired with white smoke at startup.
adVariants.cta: Worth a quick look — swing by.
